title: Comma-diagram limits construct the universal right Kan extension
statement: Work in fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain all categories and functor categories below. Let $C,D,H$ be categories [def-nagata-category], and $Q:C\to D$, $F:C\to H$ functors. For $Y\in D$ let $J_Y=(Y\downarrow Q)$ be the category with objects $(X,a:Y\to QX)$ and arrows $(X,a)\to(X',a')$ given by $f:X\to X'$ satisfying $Q(f)\circ a=a'$. Put $T_Y:J_Y\to H$, $(X,a)\mapsto F(X)$. A cone on $T_Y$ consists of an object $V$ and arrows $v_j:V\to T_Y(j)$ with $T_Y(f)v_j=v_{j'}$ for every arrow $f:j\to j'$; it is limiting if every cone factors uniquely through it. Assume $T_Y$ admits a limiting cone for every $Y\in D$. Then there are a functor $R:D\to H$ and a natural transformation $e:R\circ Q\to F$ such that $R(Y)=\lim T_Y$ and $e_X$ is the limit projection indexed by $(X,1_{QX})$. For every $G:D\to H$, the map $\operatorname{Nat}(G,R)\to\operatorname{Nat}(G\circ Q,F)$ given by $b\mapsto e\circ(bQ)$ is a bijection. Here a functor preserves identities and composition, and natural transformations are families commuting with every morphism.
